item.title: [BoSox Injection] Red Sox still haven’t ruled out last-minute activation in wake of devastating Willson Contreras news
item.dc:creator: Katie Manganelli
item.description: The Boston Red Sox on September 24 dodged a bullet with a second potential Ceddanne Rafaela injury, but got a devastating Willson Contreras update. The veteran is still feeling pain while swinging after he was hit on his right hand by a pitch and he called into question his availability for the postseason. item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox on September 24 dodged a bullet with a second potential Ceddanne Rafaela injury, but got a devastating Willson Contreras update. The veteran is still feeling pain while swinging after he was hit on his right hand by a pitch and he called into question his availability for the postseason.
The Red Sox also got an update on a long shot return candidate that could keep some hope alive. Trade deadline acquisition Curtis Mead on Friday will take batting practice off a pitching machine, according to Tim Healey of The Boston Globe (subscription required).
Mead will head to Fort Myers to join a number of players the Red Sox already have there, and Garrett Crochet will join him. Healey reports that Mead might take more batting practice off Crochet on Saturday.
The Red Sox have not formally ruled out activating Mead before the Wild Card round, which begins on September 29. It will be a close call, but there is still a slight chance that Mead could join the team before the first playoff series.
There's still a slim chance Curtis Mead could be ready for Red Sox's Wild Card series
The Red Sox dealt for Mead at the trade deadline to bring some power to their infield. The second baseman slashed .254/.352/.500 with 17 doubles and 17 home runs with the Washington Nationals. He's been on the injured list healing a fractured wrist after two at-bats in a Red Sox uniform. He hasn't appeared in a game since July 27.
There is some risk to rushing Mead back into action since he hasn't played in so long. If he does return, he'll do so without a rehab assignment because the WooSox's season has been over since September 19. If Mead isn't properly warmed up, a postseason rotation will be a rude awakening.
Still, the Red Sox's offense needs a serious lift, and even the possibility that Mead could help might be motivation enough for them to add him to the playoff roster. Boston's bats have slumped hard in September — the Red Sox have the second-lowest batting average (.221) and OPS (.656) this month and they won't get past the New York Yankees' pitching staff in that state.
Red Sox fans shouldn't get their hopes up about Mead's return. Even though he hasn't been ruled out, any blip in his recovery could cause a delay he can't come back from. He's also not as warmed up as he would be if he was returning in the regular season with a chance to go on a rehab assignment.
But Boston is desperate for a spark. If there's even a chance Mead could bring it, the Sox should let him try.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Roman Anthony rakes as Red Sox take Game 1 vs. Cubs
item.dc:creator: Jake Reiser
item.description: Alec Gamboa is not a starter. At least not at the Major League level caliber. But when the Red Sox needed someone to open a doubleheader on the last Friday of the regular season, they handed it to him anyway—and the Cubs made him pay for it quickly. item.content:encoded:
Alec Gamboa is not a starter. At least not at the Major League level caliber. But when the Red Sox needed someone to open a doubleheader on the last Friday of the regular season, they handed it to him anyway—and the Cubs made him pay for it quickly.
Tyrone Taylor doubled in the first inning to put Chicago on the board. Miguel Amaya followed with a two-run double in the second. Three runs in two innings, Clay Holmes cruising, and the Sox in a hole before most of Fenway (whoever was going to brave the risk of weather) had settled into their seats.
Then the defense took over.
Caleb Durbin threw Matt Shaw out at the plate in the second inning to keep the Cubs from stretching it further. Isiah Kiner-Falefa made a sliding grab in the third. Andruw Monasterio came up with a diving catch in the fourth. Not glamorous plays in the box score, but they kept 3-0 from turning into 5-0, and that mattered later.
Roman Anthony was (finally) doing Roman Anthony things all afternoon. He went 3-for-3 with a walk and his fingerprints are on both comeback sequences that mattered. He got things started in the third when he scored on a Dansby Swanson throwing error to make it 3-1. Stayed alive. Kept the at-bats meaningful.
It stayed there until Adley Rutschman. With two on in the fifth against Caleb Thielbar, Rutschman hit a two-run double to tie the game. That's the at-bat the rest of this recap hangs on. There's no comeback without it.
The Cubs went to Aaron Civale in the seventh. Anthony tripled to right field, then Connor Wong stepped up and hit the go-ahead double. Red Sox 4, Cubs 3.
Willson Contreras didn't play game one—his hand still won't let him swing without pain. Ceddanne Rafaela sat out too. You can file away what Boston did to Chicago's depleted lineup, but you can also file away that a team down 3-0 didn't pack it in. The seventh inning happened.
Game 2 is next. They went ahead and won the first one.
Studs
Roman Anthony — 3-for-3 with a walk. On base four times. Scored on the error in the third to keep Boston in it, tripled in the seventh to set up the go-ahead, and was just relentless all afternoon. This was his game.
Adley Rutschman — utschman's two-run double off Thielbar tied it and gave the whole thing a different shape. That's what you pay for.
Connor Wong — Go-ahead double in the seventh coming in for Mickey Gasper. Simple entry in the ledger, but a needed go-ahead run.
Dud
The first two innings — Three runs on Gamboa before anyone got comfortable. Fair amount of that is on Gamboa, fair amount is just what happens when you open with a reliever and it doesn't work. The Sox survived it. They shouldn't count on that against a full-strength playoff opponent.
The wind — How many times did the wind knock balls down today? Yes for better with potential Cubbies homers knocked down, but also it's a hamper on an already struggling offense for the Sox.
Play of the Game
Rutschman's two-run double in the fifth. Down 3-1, two runners on, Cubs holding a lead that had felt comfortable since the second inning—and Rutschman turned the whole situation. That swing is why the seventh inning got to mean something.

item.dc:creator: Cam Kerry

item.content:encoded:
Let’s play two!
With a nor’easter rolling into the area, the Cubs and Red Sox are looking to get ahead of the weather by playing a doubleheader Friday. The first game, with a 1:05 p.m. start, was originally Sunday’s contest. The teams will suit up again for a 5:35 p.m. first pitch in the nightcap — moved up slightly from its original 7:10 p.m. start, then again Thursday morning from a 6:05 start.
The Red Sox’ offense is still trying to find its form heading into October. Boston has lost four of five and has not scored more than two runs in any game during that stretch.
The Red Sox managed just two singles in Thursday’s 1-0 loss to the Guardians. In Wednesday’s 1-0 win, Andruw Monasterio snapped an 0-for-21 skid with an RBI single.
“Over these next three games, if you see some [offense] bust out, that would be great,” Red Sox manager Chad Tracy said. “We did have some quality plate appearances from certain guys, which was good to see.”
Willson Contreras sat out his sixth consecutive game. Contreras was hit in the right hand by a pitch a week ago, and said he couldn’t swing a bat the past two days. Tracy hopes to have Contreras back for postseason play when it begins Tuesday, but the first baseman gave a disappointing update about his condition.
“It’s really frustrating when you’re doing the best you can do, you’re expecting to heal faster and it doesn’t happen,” he said.
Alec Gamboa gets the nod for the Red Sox in the opener, followed by Brayan Bello in the second game. Gamboa, who has never faced the Cubs, owns a 0.50 ERA in his past 13 outings.
The Cubs are expected to start Clay Holmes and David Peterson — both midseason acquisitions from the Mets — in the Friday games.
Here’s a preview for this afternoon’s contest.
Lineups
This file will be updated with Game 2 lineups
CUBS (88-71): Crow-Armstrong CF, Suzuki RF, Bregman DH, Taylor LF, Hoerner 2B, Shaw 3B, Busch 1B, Swanson SS, Amaya C
Game 1 Pitching: RHP Clay Holmes (6-8, 3.25 ERA)
Game 2 Pitching: LHP David Peterson (9-8, 4.96 ERA)
RED SOX (85-74): Anthony LF, Gasper C, Rutschman DH, Abreu RF, Durbin 3B, Sogard 2B, Duran CF, Monasterio 1B, Kiner-Falefa SS
Game 1 Pitching: LHP Alec Gamboa (1-0, 1.16 ERA)
Game 2 Pitching: RHP Brayan Bello (6-7, 4.49 ERA)
Game 1 time: 1:05 p.m.
Game 2 time: 5:35 p.m.
TV, radio: NESN, WEEI-FM 93.7
Cubs vs. Gamboa: Has not faced any Cubs batters
Red Sox vs. Holmes: Wilyer Abreu 2-5, Willson Contreras 5-11, Jarren Duran 0-6, Isiah Kiner-Falefa 3-7, Ceddanne Rafaela 0-3, Adley Rutschman 2-4, Nick Sogard 0-2, Trevor Story 1-8, Connor Wong 1-3
Stat of the day: The Red Sox own a 39-39 record at home this season.
Notes: The Cubs downed the Marlins, 2-1, Thursday afternoon to secure their second straight postseason berth. ... Pete Crow-Armstrong became the seventh 40-homer, 40-steal player in major league history after stealing second base in the first inning. Crow-Armstrong, the National League MVP favorite, has 45 homers and 40 steals. ... The Cubs occupy the second NL wild-card spot. Chicago is a game behind the Padres and one game up on the Phillies. The top wild-card team hosts through the opening round of the playoffs.
Cam Kerry can be reached at cam.kerry@globe.com.

He's still struggling to grip a bat and admitted to tearing up out of frustration
item.content:encoded:
The Red Sox begin the postseason on Tuesday and have scored just 5 runs over the last 5 games. In other words, now would be a great time for the team's best offensive contributor to return to a lineup that desperately needs a spark. But unless a miracle happens over the weekend, things aren't looking good. Willson Contreras took batting practice on Tuesday, only for his hand injury to worsen in the subsequent days. He's still struggling to grip a bat and admitted to tearing up out of frustration. "I'm doing everything that I can to come back and play with the boys and be there with the boys," he said. "But sometimes you have to listen to your body." (Tim Healey, Boston Globe)
At least Ceddanne Rafaela has returned. He should be able to give a little lift for the lineup, though he does present a conundrum for Chad Tracy, as the Sox now have too many outfielders and DHs to fit into the lineup at once. With Roman Anthony, Rafalea, and Wilyer Abreu essentially locked into starting spots, Tracy has to decide whether to prioritize Duran's glove and legs over the platoon DH production of Mickey Gasper and Jahmai Jones. (Sean McAdam, MassLive)
And all of this is occuring against the backdrop of this weekend's storm. And if you think we're done dealing with that now that MLB has moved Sunday's game to today, we're not. There is still a possibility that one or more of this weekend's games is moved to Tropicana Field in St. Pete. (Conor Ryan, Boston.com)
With the depressing news about Contreras, the team could probably use a pep talk. If so, Pedro Martinez — as someone who still believed in this team in the darkness of May — is available. "I just feel good about approaching the Yankees this time around. And [the Red Sox] are young, yes. We don't have the highest expectations about them, but man, for some reason, I just feel so positive," said the right arm of God. "I just feel so excited that this young group of guys that we have out there are able to do something special. I don't see anything wrong with these kids, and I don't see why they shouldn't give everybody knuckles. Not just the Yankees, but everybody." (Ian Browne, MLB.com)
If the Sox are going to give everybody knuckles, then Ranger Suarez is probably going to be a part of it. The offseason signing has an outstanding postseason resume, and his final 2026 stats are more or less in line with the numbers he'd been putting up in Philadelphia, even if he sounds slightly disappointed in his performance. "Obviously I think I could have done better," he said of his season. "But I was happy I was able to finish the season strong." (Peter Abraham, Boston Globe)

item.title: [Audacy] Why Willson Contreras' hand means so much to the Red Sox
item.dc:creator: Rob Bradford
item.description: There was the 1-0 loss to the Guardians. There were the weather updates that might very well have the Red Sox and Cubs playing somewhere other than Fenway Park this weekend. And there was Ceddanne Rafaela's return from his hamstring scare. But when it came to news that mattered for the Red Sox, it was hard to top what Willson Contreras said after this latest defeat. The first baseman's bruised right hand evidently does not seem to be cooperating when it comes to postseason readiness. "I mean, it
item.content:encoded:
There was the 1-0 loss to the Guardians. There were the weather updates that might very well have the Red Sox and Cubs playing somewhere other than Fenway Park this weekend. And there was Ceddanne Rafaela's return from his hamstring scare.
But when it came to news that mattered for the Red Sox, it was hard to top what Willson Contreras said after this latest defeat.
The first baseman's bruised right hand evidently does not seem to be cooperating when it comes to postseason readiness.
"I mean, it's really concerning,” Contreras said. “But at the same time, I'm putting all my effort -- and everything I can do, I'm doing it. I don't know what else to say. I’m working hard with the trainers; the hand is slowly getting better. But I haven’t been able to swing the last two days. I’ll be honest with the team. I know Tuesday is a really important game. It's a really important series, and I'll be completely honest with the team.”
Contreras added, "It's frustrating, if I’m being honest. I was hoping to swing today, and I couldn't swing. I came into my locker just tearing up because that's what we play for. We play to play in October, and it's really frustrating when we're doing the best you can do and you're expecting to heal faster and that doesn't happen."
It appeared as though Contreras was headed in the right direction, taking an exorbitant amount of swings prior to Tuesday's game, both on the Fenway field and underneath with the Trajekt pitching machine. But the results from the exercise were not positive, with the righty hitter unable to replicate any sort of batting practice over the last couple of days.
There is still time for Contreras, with the Red Sox's first wild-card game on Tuesday. But his original plan to use the weekend games against the Cubs as a tune-up for the playoffs seems extremely unlikely.
Why is this such a big deal? It's because of the skill-set Contreras carries, one that the Red Sox seem starved for heading into the postseason.
All good postseason runs are usually built on the back of top-of-the-order power, with opponents needing to navigate their way through a team's alpha batters. Hitting home runs, in particular, is usually a top priority. The Blue Jays and Dodgers lived that life a year ago, as did the Yankees and Los Angeles the year before. You know who didn't? The 2025 Red Sox during their three wild-card games at Yankee Stadium.
Trevor Story's solo homer in Game 2 of last season's playoff showdown with the Yankees marked the only time a Red Sox player cleared the fences. It was a deficiency that was difficult to ignore.
It was why Craig Breslow proclaimed early in the offseason that his team needed more power. It was the reason acquiring Curtis Mead became a priority heading into the trade deadline. And it is why Contreras, who leads the Red Sox with 27 homers, has been so important. (The Red Sox are 18-8 when Contreras hits at least one homer.)
While this Red Sox team has taught us that things can turn in a hurry, the way the Sox's offense has been trending isn't good. In the last five games, the Sox have hit only two home runs. And in September, Chad Tracy's team has the second-lowest batting average and OPS in baseball, while scoring the fewest runs (13 fewer than the next-worst).
There are potential solutions to the Red Sox's postseason power problem, including Roman Anthony (who is tied with Mickey Gasper for the team lead in homers for September with four), Adley Rutschman, Story, Rafaela and Wilyer Abreu, who has two home runs since Aug. 16.
But Contreras has always been the constant ... until now.
“When it hurts, it hurts. Especially when it's the top hand,” Contreras said. “If it was the bottom hand, I could swing with the right hand, but when it's the right hand, my right hand just feels weaker until I just let the bat go. It's not a good sign. ... Again, I'm doing everything that I can to come back and play with the boys and be there with the boys. But sometimes you have to listen to your body, and I'm listening to the trainers and doing everything that they ask me to do, and [it's] just one of those things that I can't control."

item.title: [The Boston Globe] Chad Tracy hopes to have Willson Contreras back by the start of the playoffs - The Boston Globe
item.dc:creator: Tim Healey
item.description: Willson Contreras remained absent from the Red Sox’ lineup Thursday night at Fenway Park, seven days after he got hit by a pitch and bruised his right hand. Is it fair to say he will be ready for the start of the playoffs? “I hope so,” manager Chad Tracy said before the team’s finale with the Guardians. “I hope so. But [the Red Sox] want to see how he gets through all this stuff and where he’s at. And my hope is — at least for now — that he swings and feels even better than he did the other day,
item.content:encoded:
Willson Contreras remained absent from the Red Sox’ lineup Thursday night at Fenway Park, seven days after he got hit by a pitch and bruised his right hand.
Is it fair to say he will be ready for the start of the playoffs?
“I hope so,” manager Chad Tracy said before the team’s finale with the Guardians. “I hope so. But [the Red Sox] want to see how he gets through all this stuff and where he’s at. And my hope is — at least for now — that he swings and feels even better than he did the other day, and then we’ll go from there.”
The first baseman took batting practice in the indoor cage, as he did earlier in the week.
It would be “huge,” Tracy said, if he was ready in time to play at any point during the Cubs series. Otherwise, he may well roll into the AL Wild Card Series without having faced live pitching in nearly two weeks.
“But I also think you’re talking about a guy [who has] a pretty good idea of his swing,” Tracy said. “[With] Willson not being down that long, the most important thing is that he’s healthy. So if he’s healthy and feeling good about it, where we’re able to get him some at-bats, that’d be great. But we’re still going to be reactive to how he’s feeling.”
Weather watch
The Cubs-Red Sox series remains in flux.
They will attempt to play a doubleheader at Fenway Park on Friday, with 1 p.m. and 6 p.m. first pitches, before a potential nor’easter arrives.
Yet to be decided: where and when the teams play their regular-season finale. Although it is scheduled for 7:15 p.m. Saturday in Boston, it could be moved to another venue, such as Tampa Bay, if the weekend forecast remains horrendous.
If the game is moved, the clubs would leave Friday night and likely play at 3 p.m. Sunday, same as all of the other finales.
MLB and the teams intend to make a call by midday Friday about what to do about Game 162.
“In a nutshell, it doesn’t look good. That’s basically what I’ve heard,” Tracy said of the weather. “Seems like we should be able to get that [doubleheader] in even [if during] the second game there might be a little bit of drizzle or whatever. It doesn’t look bad, at least what I’m seeing, and then figure out what happens next.”
Crochet on the move
A wrinkle from the weather: Garrett Crochet (left shoulder injury) will head to Fort Myers, Fla., on Friday so that he can throw an inning of live batting practice on Saturday.
The Sox have a stash of Triple-A hitters, including infielders Romy Gonzalez and Franklin Arias, working out at Fenway South.
Rafaela OK
Ceddanne Rafaela turned out to be just fine after a scare Wednesday.
The Thursday MRI on his right hamstring came back “clean,” Tracy said, affirming Rafaela’s stance from the night prior that his exit after two innings was no big deal.
“The feel is that it was a cramp, probably actually precipitated by the diving catch an inning prior],” Tracy said. “He tends to dive, and he does have low back/hip stuff that throws him out of the line for a second, that’ll manifest itself in feeling [the hamstring].”
Rafaela was back in the lineup against the Guardians, batting sixth and playing center field. It was his second game back from a right quad strain.
Major honors from minors
The Red Sox announced their annual minor league award winners, a group headed by Arias, the offensive player of the year. He slashed .323/.400/.557 with 25 homers and 91 RBIs in 117 games with Double-A Portland and Triple-A Worcester, emerging as one of the top prospects in all of the minors.
Lefthander Dylan Brown was named pitcher of the year. A 22-year-old starter, he had a 3.46 ERA and 143 strikeouts in 106⅔ innings with Low-A Salem and High-A Greenville.
Other honored were catcher Gerardo Rodriguez (defensive player of the year), outfielder Andrews Opata (baserunner of the year), outfielder Joskairo Ramirez (Latin program position player of the year), and righthander Emanuel Jimenez (Latin program pitcher of the year).
Mead update
Infielder Curtis Mead (left wrist fracture) plans to take another step forward Friday by taking batting practice off of a machine. He will head to Fort Myers with Crochet and potentially hit against him on Saturday, he said. He is not ruled out for the first round of the playoffs beginning Tuesday, but that deadline might be too soon … Tracy left Roman Anthony out of the lineup to give him a day off. The outfielder had started 22 consecutive games since returning from the IL, batting .242 with a .726 OPS … Eli White was back at Fenway for the first time since season-ending right foot surgery Tuesday. He said he is due for a three-month recovery. That timeline would allow the outfielder to get almost all the way back to full health before the expected lockout on Dec. 1, at which point teams will not be allowed to communicate with players … Infielder Anthony Seigler said he was diagnosed with a carpal boss, a bony lump on the back of his right hand/wrist — the same injury that plagued catcher Connor Wong last year. Wong wound up having surgery to get it removed. Seigler said he has not discussed that possibility with the Red Sox … DH/outfielder Masataka Yoshida (left hamstring strain) appeared on the field at Fenway, playing catch and doing light agility drills … Dustin Pedroia and his family, in town this week, were on the field about five hours before first pitch against Cleveland, chatting with Red Sox personnel. His three sons made sure to poke their head into the Green Monster.
Tim Healey can be reached at timothy.healey@globe.com. Follow him @timbhealey.

item.title: [bostonherald.com] Red Sox outfielder in lineup after leaving Wednesday with hamstring issue
item.dc:creator: Mac Cerullo
item.description: Ceddanne Rafaela is back in the Red Sox lineup a day after leaving Wednesday night’s game with a right hamstring tightness. The Red Sox outfielder will bat sixth and start in center field for Thursday night’s finale against the Cleveland Guardians. “He’s good,” Red Sox manager Chad Tracy said pregame Thursday. “All the scans last night were clean, we did an MRI as a precaution, all clean, subjectively he feels really good, so seems exactly what it was, the feel is it was a cramp.” Rafaela left W
item.content:encoded:
Ceddanne Rafaela is back in the Red Sox lineup a day after leaving Wednesday night’s game with a right hamstring tightness.
The Red Sox outfielder will bat sixth and start in center field for Thursday night’s finale against the Cleveland Guardians.
“He’s good,” Red Sox manager Chad Tracy said pregame Thursday. “All the scans last night were clean, we did an MRI as a precaution, all clean, subjectively he feels really good, so seems exactly what it was, the feel is it was a cramp.”
Rafaela left Wednesday’s game in the top of the third inning after initially feeling tightness during his first at bat in the bottom of the second. He had just been activated from the injured list earlier that day after missing 17 games with a right quad strain, though Rafaela expressed optimism postgame that the hamstring issue was far less serious.
Losing Rafaela again so soon before the playoffs would have been a huge blow to the Red Sox. The outfielder is a favorite to win his second Gold Glove in center field and has enjoyed a strong season at the plate, batting .284 with 16 home runs, 17 stolen bases and a .763 OPS.
Though Rafaela won’t miss any more time, Willson Contreras remains out of the lineup with a bruised hand after being hit by a pitch last Thursday in Texas. Contreras has now been sidelined for a week, and the plan was for him to run through a battery of hitting drills in the cages and on the field Thursday to see how his hand is progressing.
While the hope is he will be ready to return soon, Tracy acknowledged that isn’t a guarantee.
“I hope so, but I want to see how he gets through all this stuff and where he’s at, and my hope is at least for now that he feels even better than he did the other day and we’ll go from there.”
Tracy added that while it would be great for Contreras to get some at bats before the regular season ends, he hasn’t missed much time and has a good idea of his swing, so it wouldn’t be an issue if he didn’t play before the postseason.
“The most important thing is he’s healthy,” Tracy said. “So if he’s healthy and feeling good about it where we can get him some at bats, that’d be great, but we’re still going to be reactive to how he’s feeling.”
Minor League awards
Top prospect Franklin Arias highlighted the Red Sox minor league award winners, earning Offensive Player of the Year recognition. The 20-year-old shortstop enjoyed a dominant season in which he batted .323 with 25 home runs, 91 RBI and a .957 OPS over 117 games across Double-A and Triple-A, and he finishes the year ranked as MLB’s No. 2 prospect according to Baseball America.
The other recipients include left-hander Dylan Brown (Pitcher of the Year), catcher Gerardo Rodriguez (Defensive Player of the Year), outfielder Andrews Opata (Baserunner of the Year), outfielder Joskairo Ramirez (Latin Program Position Player of the Year) and right-hander Emanuel Jimenez (Latin Program Pitcher of the Year).
Right-hander Wyatt Olds is also being recognized as the 2026 recipient of the Lou Gorman Award, which annually honors a Red Sox minor leaguer who demonstrates perseverance to make his big league debut.
Extra innings
With heavy rain expected throughout the weekend the Red Sox plan to send left-hander Garrett Crochet to Fort Myers on Friday so he can throw his next live batting practice session on Saturday. The expectation is he will throw one inning but probably more pitches than the 16 he threw on Tuesday. Depending on how things go the club will decide whether or not to add him to the Wild Card roster. … Roman Anthony, who is also not in Thursday’s lineup, is being given a day off his feet to rest, Tracy said. … Back in the clubhouse wearing a walking boot following his foot surgery earlier this week, outfielder Eli White confirmed he’ll be non-weight bearing for several weeks and will miss the remainder of the season. … Infielder Anthony Seigler (right wrist inflammation) has resumed taking ground balls and ran through a series of drills Thursday. … The Red Sox have not determined who will start Game 1 and 2 of next week’s AL Wild Card Series.

item.title: [sunjournal.com] Red Sox center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela leaves game with hamstring tightness
item.dc:creator: Scott Martin

He singled off the Green Monster in the second inning and came up lame at first b
item.content:encoded:
BOSTON — Red Sox center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela, who came off the injured list on Wednesday, left the game against the Cleveland Guardians before the third inning after pulling up while running out a single in the second.
Rafaela, who started and made a diving catch on the game’s first batter, had been sidelined since Sept. 3 with a right quad strain.
The team announced that he left with right hamstring tightness.
He singled off the Green Monster in the second inning and came up lame at first base. He was visited by manager Chad Tracy and a trainer, jogged a bit down the right-field foul line and stayed in the game.
He then trotted out to his position for the top of the third, but came walking off. He was replaced by Jarren Duran.
“He had like a little tightness in the upper hamstring, more on the swing,” Tracy said after their 1-0 victory over the Guardians. “I still saw him kind of flexing it a little bit (when he was heading to center), so I said ‘Let’s get him out of there.’ Everything so far is OK, they are going to get an MRI (Thursday) just to rule out anything.”
Rafaela, who won his first Gold Glove last season, made a headlong dive to rob Steve Kwan in right center on the third pitch of the game. He handled all three putouts the first inning.
“I was excited since (Tuesday) to be back on the field with the boys, then with the swing I felt a little bit of a cramp,” he said. “I was not happy.”
He said he still felt it a bit when he went to center.
“The sensation was there, it was just a cramp,” he said. “After that, I got in (the clubhouse) and did what I needed to do, and right now I feel much better.”
He was batting .284 with 16 homers and 70 RBI coming into Wednesday’s game.
To make room for him, the club optioned INF/OF Nate Eaton to Triple-A Worcester.
THE RED SOX are adjusting the schedule of their weekend series against the Chicago Cubs because of a significant storm that’s expected to bring heavy rain and strong winds to the Boston area.
The team said it was moving the Sunday afternoon game to Friday to create a split doubleheader. The first game is scheduled to begin at 1:05 p.m. The originally scheduled 7:05 p.m. night game was moved up to 6:05.
The Red Sox said in a press release Wednesday that the change was made in consultation with Major League Baseball.
The Cubs are currently in a tight race for one of the NL’s three wild-card spots.
There was no mention of a change to Saturday’s game, which is slated for a 7:15 p.m. first pitch.

item.content:encoded:
Roman Anthony is out of the Boston Red Sox lineup, raising an immediate question about whether something is wrong with the young star.
Here’s why Anthony is out of the lineup and what his absence means for the Red Sox.
Anthony is out of the Boston Red Sox lineup Thursday against Cleveland, but the club has not attached any new injury news to the decision.
Thursday is Anthony’s first day off since he returned from the injured list. The Red Sox have just three regular-season games left to play after Thursday.
| BOSTON RED SOX STARTING LINEUP | | | | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SP: Ranger Suárez (LHP #55) • 8-4, 3.27 ERA, 135 K | | | | |
| September 24, 2026 • Fenway Park, Boston, MA • 6:45 PM EDT • Guardians at Red Sox | | | | |
| # | Player | Pos | AVG | OPS |
| 1 | Nick Sogard | 1B | .258 | .740 |
| 2 | Mickey Gasper | DH | .258 | .840 |
| 3 | Adley Rutschman | C | .240 | .734 |
| 4 | Wilyer Abreu | RF | .253 | .786 |
| 5 | Caleb Durbin | 3B | .252 | .720 |
| 6 | Ceddanne Rafaela | CF | .284 | .763 |
| 7 | Jarren Duran | LF | .207 | .629 |
| 8 | Trevor Story | SS | .243 | .635 |
| 9 | Isiah Kiner-Falefa | 2B | .242 | .632 |
| Season stats shown (AVG / OPS). | | | | |
Roman Anthony’s Lineup Status for Guardians Series Finale
Manager Chad Tracy had not yet explained the absence when the club posted the lineup ahead of his pregame media session.
The rest of the card shows how the night is built. Jarren Duran starts in left field, Mickey Gasper takes the designated hitter spot and Ceddanne Rafaela returns to center. Gasper bats right-handed, and Cleveland counters with right-hander Daniel Espino, according to MLB.com‘s lineup page. Left-hander Ranger Suarez (8-4, 3.27 ERA) starts for Boston.
Rafaela left Wednesday’s 1-0 win with right hamstring tightness and was set to undergo an MRI Thursday, according to the Boston Globe. Duran replaced Rafaela in the third inning and went 2-for-3, according to the Globe‘s recap. Willson Contreras sits again.
Gasper was among the players optioned to make room for Anthony’s return.
“It was bittersweet. Like, I really mean it,” Tracy said, as quoted by Yahoo Sports.
Boston has already clinched a playoff spot. Tuesday’s card benched Trevor Story, Duran and Contreras with no public explanation, according to NESN reporter Rodney Knuppel.
| CLEVELAND GUARDIANS STARTING LINEUP | | | | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SP: Daniel Espino (RHP #41) • 0-0, 4.73 ERA, 22 K | | | | |
| September 24, 2026 • Fenway Park, Boston, MA • 6:45 PM EDT • Guardians at Red Sox | | | | |
| # | Player | Pos | AVG | OPS |
| 1 | Steven Kwan | CF | .282 | .725 |
| 2 | José Ramírez | 3B | .235 | .694 |
| 3 | Chase DeLauter | RF | .290 | .819 |
| 4 | Jo Adell | DH | .240 | .694 |
| 5 | Angel Martínez | LF | .258 | .761 |
| 6 | David Fry | 1B | .192 | .661 |
| 7 | Travis Bazzana | 2B | .245 | .741 |
| 8 | Patrick Bailey | C | .207 | .592 |
| 9 | Brayan Rocchio | SS | .250 | .690 |
| Season stats shown (AVG / OPS). | | | | |
Boston Red Sox Playoff Plans for Roman Anthony
No report ties Thursday’s absence to the right ring finger that cost Anthony nearly four months. He left a May 4 game at Detroit with wrist and hand discomfort, later described as a partially torn ligament, according to NESN‘s injury timeline.
Rehab stalled. Anthony “hasn’t made any substantive progress,” Tracy said in a late-June update, as quoted by Boston.com.
The Red Sox shifted him to the 60-day list and sent him to Fort Myers. Even after 3 1/2 months, the club declined to circle a return date, according to the Boston Globe. He was finally activated on Aug. 30, according to NBC Sports.
He has hit .242/.294/.432 with four home runs in 22 games since activation. His return began 10-for-22 over five games, then cooled to .137/.214/.296 across 56 plate appearances through Sept. 18. That night at Tampa Bay he hit a 438-foot leadoff homer, according to CBS Sports. He went 0-for-5 Tuesday and 1-for-4 Wednesday, according to CBS Sports‘ game log.
Tracy has resisted singling out Anthony during cold stretches.
“It’s not a Roman thing,” he said in May, as quoted by The Boston Globe.
Anthony wants the October he missed in 2025 with an oblique injury, and he said he is “where I want to be,” as quoted by The Boston Globe. The AL wild-card series opens Tuesday.
Anthony remains active and available off the bench. Any appearance Thursday would likely come as a pinch hitter, a role for his left-handed bat late in the game.

item.content:encoded:
Sep 24, 2026, 3:16 PM ET
Boston Red Sox first baseman Willson Contreras (hand) is missing a sixth straight game in Thursday's series finale against the visiting Cleveland Guardians, per MLB.com. Nick Sogard is making another start at first base and will bat out of the leadoff spot against Guardians right-hander Daniel Espino. Contreras was hit by a pitch on his right hand in last Thursday's game against the Texas Rangers. X-rays came back negative, but Boston has elected to give him some extra rest with the postseason starting next week. We would expect Contreras to return during this weekend's series at home against the Chicago Cubs. The four-time All-Star has hit a career-high 27 home runs while driving in 81 runs in 129 games across 533 plate appearances, but he has only played in four games in September after hitting only .217 (18-for-83) with three homers, 11 walks, and 26 strikeouts in 23 games in August. The Red Sox will need Contreras, who has been one of their most consistent hitters for the majority of the 2026 season, in top form if they want to make a deep playoff run.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
More Recent News
Sep 24, 2026, 3:16 PM ET
Miami Marlins infield prospect Jacob Lombard's first taste of professional baseball was a mixed bag while playing for Single-A Jupiter. The Marlins' fourth-ranked prospect hit four home runs, stole 11 bases, and registered a 13.1 percent walk rate in 22 games for the Hammerheads. He also propelled the team to the Florida State League playoffs (which they went on to win) by hitting a go-ahead home run with the team down to its final strike of the season, then went 5-for-14 (.357) with a pair of home runs during the playoffs. The downside was that he hit just .220 during the regular season, due largely to an astronomical 39.4 percent strikeout rate. If the 2026 first-round draft pick can make progress in that area next season, he should see time at High-A and perhaps even Double-A by season's end. At just 18 years old, it will be a few years before he debuts in the majors, but there is plenty of upside here to make him a worthy stash in dynasty leagues.--Jarod Rupp
Source: MiLB.com
Ceddanne Rafaela Back in Boston's Lineup


Keith Hernandez




Sep 24, 2026, 3:10 PM ET
Boston Red Sox outfielder Ceddanne Rafaela (hamstring) is starting in center field and batting sixth for Thursday's series finale against the visiting Cleveland Guardians and right-hander Daniel Espino, according to MLB.com. Rafaela returned from a stay on the injured list due to a quadriceps injury but was pulled on Wednesday night against the Guardians with tightness in his hamstring. An MRI exam on Thursday morning apparently ruled out anything concerning, and the power/speed threat and starting center fielder is back in action for the final game of the series at Fenway Park. It is great news for the Red Sox, who did not want to head into the start of the postseason next week without their starting center fielder. The 26-year-old will now have four games to try to set a new career-high mark in home runs, as he enters Thursday's action with 16 homers, 70 RBI, 17 stolen bases, 67 runs scored, and a .284/.319/.444 slash line in 536 at-bats this year. Rafaela was a first-time All-Star this year in his third full season in the big leagues.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
Sep 24, 2026, 3:06 PM ET
Miami Marlins outfield prospect Cam Cannarella tore through the Miami farm system this season on his way to Triple-A, logging just 19 games at High-A, then only 34 at Double-A before earning the promotion to the minors' highest level. Although his strikeout rate spiked from 12.9 percent at the lower levels to 23.8 percent while at Jacksonville, the Marlins' sixth-ranked prospect maintained a strong walk rate of 14.1 percent and still hit .282 with an .813 OPS to go along with three home runs and 11 steals in 45 games with the Jumbo Shrimp. In all, he hit 15 home runs across all three levels, not bad for someone who doesn't have a highly rated power tool, so it's something to keep an eye on in 2027. If the 23-year-old can continue to produce home runs to go with his penchant for contact and a keen eye, not to mention his plus speed, there could be a valuable fantasy asset here who would be on the verge of making his MLB debut next year.--Jarod Rupp
Source: MiLB.com
Sep 24, 2026, 2:55 PM ET
Baltimore Orioles outfield prospect Ike Irish (knee) was enjoying his first full season of professional baseball earlier this year while playing for High-A Fredericksburg. The former first-round draft pick had really heated up before a torn left meniscus ended his season in late July. The Orioles' fifth-ranked prospect batted .361 with nine doubles, a triple, seven home runs, and nine steals over his final 26 games before the injury. The hot stretch pushed his season-long slash line to .286/.388/.528 with 16 home runs and 20 steals in just 76 games for the Keys. The left-handed hitter recently returned to the diamond and will head to the Arizona Fall League to make up for lost time. As such, he should be fully healthy come spring and looks ready to spend much of the 2027 season at Double-A. He likely won't make his major league debut until 2028, but the 22-year-old has shown good contact, plenty of power, and an ability to steal bases despite not having a ton of speed, so his dynasty arrow is pointing way up for the potential to impact multiple fantasy categories.--Jarod Rupp
Source: MiLB.com
Liam Doyle Finishes 2026 on a High Note


Jarod Rupp




Sep 24, 2026, 2:37 PM ET
St. Louis Cardinals pitching prospect Liam Doyle capped off his 2026 season with a strong start in the Double-A Texas League Championship on Wednesday, allowing just one run (zero earned) on four hits and two walks while striking out six batters in five innings of work. It followed his earlier playoff start in which the left-hander gave up just one earned run on no hits and five walks while striking out eight batters in only 3 2/3 innings pitched. The former fifth-overall draft pick spent the entirety of the 2026 regular season at Double-A Springfield, recording a 3.76 ERA, 1.31 WHIP, and a 17.6 percent K-BB% in 23 starts (130 K in 103 IP). His performance this year puts the Cards' top pitching prospect on track for Triple-A in 2027 and a possible MLB debut at some point next year. If there is one criticism, it is that his walk rate remained elevated throughout the season, coming in at 12.5 percent, but so long as the 6-foot-2 hurler can keep striking out batters at a high clip, then it shouldn't get in the way of moving up the ladder. The 22-year-old remains a strong dynasty stash.--Jarod Rupp
Source: MiLB.com
Sep 24, 2026, 2:29 PM ET
Colorado Rockies corner infield/outfield prospect Charlie Condon capped off a strong 2026 season by smacking a home run in his final game of the year. The Rockies' third-ranked prospect finished with 27 long balls in 130 games played, while batting .273 with a stellar .390 on-base percentage thanks to a 13.2 percent walk rate. The former third-overall draft pick continued to strike out at a high rate of 25.1 percent, though that isn't that out of the ordinary for a guy who has as much power as he does. The 6-foot-5 slugger surprisingly never got the call to the majors this year despite a few very hot stretches of production, but that doesn't mean he won't be in the mix for a roster spot in 2027. The 23-year-old has a shot to make the team out of camp next year, and even if he doesn't, expect him to be one of the first high-profile prospect names called up in 2027. The strikeouts could make him a batting-average risk for fantasy, but the pop he possesses will play well at Coors Field, and the right-handed hitter is still a solid dynasty investment.--Jarod Rupp
Source: MiLB.com
Sep 24, 2026, 2:11 PM ET
Tampa Bay Rays outfield prospect Theo Gillen recorded a strong 2026 season, one that began at High-A and finished at Double-A. The Rays' second-ranked prospect was promoted to Double-A after 57 games at High-A, and despite a dip in batting average from .342 to .288, he did not appear to be overmatched. The former first-rounder's strikeout rate actually improved there, from 23.8 percent to 19.8 percent, while his walk rate remained steady. All in all, the 6-foot-2 slugger slashed .315/.419/.546 with 22 home runs and 44 steals in 116 games and moved all the way up to No. 12 on MLB.com's top prospects list. His type of all-around skill set makes the left-handed hitter a valuable dynasty asset, and he'll have his sights set on Triple-A next year. Once he's knocking on the door to the major leagues, which could be as soon as later next season, even redraft managers should be keeping a close eye on him.--Jarod Rupp
Source: MiLB.com
Kevin Gausman Unsure When he Might Pitch Again


Keith Hernandez




Sep 24, 2026, 1:42 PM ET
Chicago Cubs veteran right-hander Kevin Gausman (shoulder) said his left shoulder is still sore from the diving play he made at third base in the loss to the Miami Marlins on Wednesday night at Wrigley Field, according to Bruce Levine of 670 The Score. Gausman is getting treatment, but he would not predict his availability to pitch in the wild-card series next week. The 35-year-old is now up in the air as an option to pitch for the Cubbies in Game 1 of the wild-card series next week against an undetermined opponent. In his final regular-season start of 2026 on Wednesday night, Gausman allowed two earned runs on six hits (one homer) while walking one and striking out seven in 5 2/3 innings in a no-decision. He had a 4.38 ERA and 1.29 WHIP in 23 starts with the Toronto Blue Jays to begin the year before being traded to the Cubs at the deadline in early August. Gausman was not quite as good in nine starts with Chicago, going 4-2 with a 4.83 ERA, 1.23 WHIP, and 57:11 K:BB in 50 1/3 innings pitched.--Keith Hernandez
Source: 670 The Score - Bruce Levine
Sandy Alcantara Will Not Start This Weekend


Keith Hernandez




Sep 24, 2026, 1:35 PM ET
Miami Marlins manager Clayton McCullough said on Thursday that right-hander Sandy Alcantara will not make one more start this weekend against the division-rival Atlanta Braves, according to Stephen Strom. However, Alcantara, who picked up another save in the win over the Chicago Cubs at Wrigley Field on Wednesday night, will continue to be available out of the bullpen. Alcantara is 100% healthy, but McCullough said he felt like it was the right time to give the right-hander a breather with the season coming to an end this weekend. Going into Thursday's series finale against Chicago, the 31-year-old Dominican has gone 13-11 on the year with a 3.89 ERA (4.09 FIP) and 1.23 WHIP with 152 strikeouts and 59 walks in a league-high and career-high 213 innings pitched across 35 appearances (33 starts). Although he will not make another start this week, Alcantara could still help fantasy managers vying for a championship if he continues to work as a high-leverage reliever in save situations with regular closer Pete Fairbanks (hand) done for the season.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Stephen Strom
Ceddanne Rafaela Undergoing MRI Exam on his Hamstring


Keith Hernandez




Sep 24, 2026, 1:27 PM ET
Boston Red Sox outfielder Ceddanne Rafaela (hamstring) is undergoing an MRI exam on Thursday on his injured right hamstring, manager Chad Tracy told Tim Healey of The Boston Globe. In his return from a quadriceps injury on Wednesday that had landed him on the injured list, Rafaela was pulled from the contest against the Cleveland Guardians with tightness in his right hamstring. The Red Sox are hoping it was just a cramping issue, but we will know for sure at some point on Thursday. Fantasy managers should not expect the starting center fielder to be back in action for Thursday's series finale against the Guardians at Fenway Park, but hopefully Rafaela will be ready to return for Friday's series opener against the visiting Chicago Cubs. The 26-year-old was a first-time All-Star in 2026 and is currently slashing a healthy .284/.319/.444 with a .763 OPS, 16 home runs, 70 RBI, 17 stolen bases, and 67 runs scored across his 136 games played. If Rafaela can return before the end of the weekend, he will have a chance to set a new career high in home runs.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Boston Globe - Tim Healey
Xavier Edwards Remains Out of Marlins' Lineup


Keith Hernandez




Sep 24, 2026, 1:21 PM ET
Miami Marlins middle infielder Xavier Edwards (thumb) continues to sit for Thursday's series finale at Wrigley Field against the Chicago Cubs, per MLB.com. Jared Serna will make the start at the keystone for the Fish and will bat eighth against Cubs left-hander Matthew Boyd. The 27-year-old Edwards injured his thumb on Saturday against the San Diego Padres and has not played since. With the Marlins eliminated from postseason contention, they might elect to sit Edwards for the rest of the final week of the regular season. He has minimal power, but Edwards is a spark plug because of his speed and contact skills, and he is currently hitting .280/.360/.371 with a .730 OPS, a career-high six home runs, 52 RBI, 21 stolen bases, and 61 runs scored across 142 games played and 595 plate appearances in just his second full season in the majors. Edwards' next chance to return to the lineup will be in Friday's series opener in Miami against the division-rival Atlanta Braves.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
Sep 24, 2026, 11:58 AM ET
Across 182 innings (31 starts) in 2026, Seattle Mariners starting pitcher Logan Gilbert has recorded a 12-11 record with a 3.81 ERA, 1.10 WHIP, and 197 strikeouts. While Gilbert has still been a very useful pitcher for fantasy managers, he hasn't been quite as dominant this season as he has been in his peak years. After posting a 32.3% strikeout rate in 2025, Gilbert's strikeout rate has fallen to 26.7% in 2026. The 29-year-old's numbers have taken a considerable hit lately, as he's posted a 6.65 ERA across 21 2/3 innings in September. Surrendering the long ball has been a major issue for Gilbert in the second half of the season. Across 56 1/3 innings (10 starts) since the beginning of August, Gilbert has allowed 14 home runs (2.20 HR/9). Heading into his final scheduled start of 2026 against the Los Angeles Angels on Sunday, fantasy managers may want to temper expectations for the usually dependable Gilbert.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller
Sep 24, 2026, 11:47 AM ET
Across 653 plate appearances in 2026, San Diego Padres outfielder Jackson Merrill is hitting .252/.300/.459 with 26 home runs, 86 RBI, 82 runs scored, and 26 stolen bases. The 23-year-old got off to a rough start to the year, hitting .219 with 10 home runs across 396 plate appearances before the All-Star break. However, Merrill has been red hot in the second half, hitting .300 with 16 homers across his last 261 trips to the plate. Merrill has been particularly key to San Diego's late-season surge as an offense, hitting .325 with four home runs, 16 RBI, 10 runs scored, and two stolen bases over his first 85 plate appearances in September. The star center fielder has lowered his strikeout rate this month to 18.8% while also posting elite barrel (19.7%) and hard-hit (62.1%) rates. Heading into San Diego's final weekend of the regular season, Merrill profiles as one of the top five-category producers in all of fantasy baseball.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller
Sep 24, 2026, 11:33 AM ET
Across 102 innings (19 starts) in 2026, Houston Astros right-hander Hunter Brown has recorded a 6-3 record with a 3.26 ERA, 1.27 WHIP, and 120 strikeouts. The 28-year-old got off to a rough start to the year, missing over two months with a shoulder injury and posting a 4.94 ERA across 27 1/3 innings in July. However, Brown has begun to rediscover his top form in recent outings. Across his last 33 1/3 innings (six starts), Brown is 3-0 with a 2.43 ERA, 1.20 WHIP, and 48 strikeouts. Brown has had issues with command all year long, and his 11.9% walk rate has led to an elevated WHIP. However, he's boosted his strikeout rate all the way up to 28.1% and has struck out 39.1% of the batters he's faced across his first four starts of September. Heading into his final start of the regular season on Saturday against the Athletics, Brown is beginning to look like the fantasy ace he was drafted to be ahead of 2026.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller
Sep 24, 2026, 11:21 AM ET
Across 501 plate appearances in 2026, Cleveland Guardians second baseman Travis Bazzana is hitting .245/.337/.404 with 15 home runs, 57 RBI, 53 runs scored, and 19 stolen bases. The 24-year-old's underlying batted-ball metrics are underwhelming, as he's logged just a 4.8% barrel rate and a 36.2% hard-hit rate. However, Bazzana's 11.2% walk rate is impressive for a young player and helps him get on base consistently and use his speed. Bazzana has also been red-hot of late, hitting .288 with six home runs, 15 RBI, and 11 runs scored across 69 plate appearances in September. If the former top prospect is starting to grow into his power, he could begin to emerge as one of the better second base options for fantasy managers. In leagues where he's on the waiver wire, Bazzana should be a priority target for fantasy managers.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller
Sep 24, 2026, 11:15 AM ET
Across 655 plate appearances in 2026, Minnesota Twins first baseman Josh Bell is hitting .255/.317/.416 with 20 home runs, 92 RBI, 76 runs scored, and two stolen bases. The 34-year-old may not have one clear standout skill, but he remains a steady source of power and run production. Bell has kept his strikeout rate manageable at 19.9% while still posting solid barrel (9.5%) and hard-hit (42.0%) rates. The veteran switch-hitter also remains locked into everyday playing time in the heart of the Twins lineup, putting him in a good position to rack up runs and RBI. Heading into the final weekend of the regular season, Bell profiles as a balanced producer for fantasy managers to target on the waiver wire.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller
Sep 24, 2026, 11:10 AM ET
Across 444 plate appearances in 2026, Baltimore Orioles third baseman/first baseman Coby Mayo is hitting .225/.293/.463 with 24 home runs, 63 RBI, 63 runs scored, and four stolen bases. Swing-and-miss is the obvious red flag in Mayo's profile, as he's struck out in 30.2% of his plate appearances. However, the 24-year-old brings significant power upside with a 13.7% barrel rate and a 47.6% hard-hit rate. Mayo has hit .265 with 12 home runs since the All-Star break, and he's established himself as an everyday presence in the heart of the Baltimore lineup. For fantasy managers in need of power, Mayo profiles as a priority target on the waiver wire heading into the final weekend of the regular season.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller
Carlos Lagrange Could Join Yankees' Playoff Roster


Keith Hernandez




Sep 24, 2026, 12:02 AM ET
New York Yankees manager Aaron Boone said that right-handed pitching prospect Carlos Lagrange is "in the conversation" for a spot on the team's postseason roster for the wild-card series next week against the division-rival Boston Red Sox, according to Gary Phillips of the New York Daily News. The 23-year-old Dominican is the team's No. 3 prospect at MLB Pipeline, and he has been ramping up his throwing program since coming off the seven-day injured list on Sept. 16 with a sprained right shoulder. Lagrange went 1-4 this year at Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre, recording a 4.48 ERA, 1.35 WHIP, and 85:33 K:BB in 64 1/3 innings pitched across 19 appearances (11 starts). If Lagrange is pulled up to the Yankees' playoff roster, he would be making his major-league debut in the postseason in a relief role out of the bullpen. The 6-foot-7, 248-pounder has the tools to excel in high-leverage spots with an upper-90s fastball with armside run and multiple secondary pitches that can generate swings and misses consistently.--Keith Hernandez
Source: New York Daily News - Gary Phillips
Sep 23, 2026, 11:52 PM ET
Chicago Cubs right-hander Kevin Gausman (shoulder) came up wincing and in some apparent pain after diving to tag a runner out at third base during his start on Wednesday at Wrigley Field against the visiting Miami Marlins, according to Tony Andracki. Gausman was pulled from the game, but he was also at 101 pitches on the night. Manager Craig Counsell said that Gausman's left shoulder got extended awkwardly and "grabbed on him" on the play. He is now sore, and the Cubs will see how he feels in the next couple of days. Gausman is lined up to potentially start Game 1 or 2 next week in the wild-card series in the playoffs. The good news for the Cubs is that the injury is to the veteran's non-throwing arm as well. He came one out shy of a quality start for his fantasy managers on Wednesday, allowing two earned runs on six hits (one homer) while walking one and striking out seven in 5 2/3 frames for a no-decision. The 35-year-old veteran came into his final start of the regular season with a 9-12 record, 4.55 ERA, 1.27 WHIP, and 177 strikeouts in 172 innings pitched in 2026 with the Cubs and Toronto Blue Jays.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Tony Andracki
Sep 23, 2026, 10:59 PM ET
New York Yankees manager Aaron Boone said that shortstop/second baseman Anthony Volpe could see some playing time at third base this week, per the Talkin' Yanks podcast. Volpe has mostly played shortstop in his MLB career, but he recently filled in at second base while Yankees second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. was sidelined by a thumb injury. With Chisholm Jr. back, it appears that New York could work Volpe into the mix at third base. The Yankees have gotten underwhelming production at the hot corner from Ryan McMahon, who has hit .210 with 11 home runs across 356 plate appearances in 2026. Volpe's numbers don't appear much better on the surface, as he's hit .244/.321/.335 with two home runs, 26 RBI, 24 runs scored, and 11 stolen bases across 234 plate appearances. However, the 25-year-old has been better in September, hitting .263 with four stolen bases across 40 trips to the plate this month.--Will Brady
Source: Talkin' Yanks

item.content:encoded:
With the coming nor’easter hitting town this weekend, the Red Sox and Guardians have played with an October chill in the air this week.
The Red Sox halted their three-game slide with a 1-0 win on Wednesday. Andrew Monasterio’s RBI single in the bottom of the sixth held as the eventual winner after Sonny Gray dealt six shutout innings.
That came after the Guardians won Tuesday’s contest, 3-2, setting up Thursday’s game as the series rubber match.
Given his postgame comments, the Red Sox hope to have avoided a scare regarding center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela, who left his first game back from the injured list with right hamstring tightness. A quad injury sent him to the IL on Sept. 3.
“Not even close,” Rafaela said of the severity comparison of the two injuries. “I think it was just a cramp.”
After the game, Tracy said Rafaela would have an MRI exam on Thursday.
Ranger Suarez will start for the Red Sox on Thursday. He’s 1-1 with a 4.00 ERA in four career appearances, including three starts, against Cleveland. On May 31, he struck out 10 and allowed four runs across five frames against Cleveland in Boston’s 9-4 win.
“He’s a very good competitor, a good pitcher that even when he gets traffic, you trust that he’s going to find his way through it,” Tracy said of Suarez, whose ERA in three September starts is 0.92.
Daniel Espino will open for Cleveland before giving way to Joey Cantillo.
Here’s a preview of Thursday’s action.
Lineups
GUARDIANS (82-76): TBA
Pitching: RHP Daniel Espino (0-0, 4.73 ERA)
RED SOX (85-73): TBA
Pitching: LHP Ranger Suarez (8-4, 3.27 ERA)
Time: 6:45 p.m.
TV, radio: NESN, WEEI-FM 93.7
Guardians vs. Suarez: Jo Adell 2-5, Travis Bazzana 0-3, Chase DeLauter 2-3, David Fry 4-5, Austin Hedges 1-4, Steven Kwan 1-6, Nathaniel Lowe 1-6, Angel Martínez 0-2, José Ramírez 5-8, Brayan Rocchio 1-2
Red Sox vs. Espino: Has not faced any Boston batters
Stat of the day: The Red Sox have notched an American League-leading 17 shutouts this season.
Notes: The Guardians are on the verge of sealing their postseason berth. Cleveland’s magic number is just one, the same as their AL Central rival, the White Sox. If both win on Thursday, they both will earn a postseason berth. ... Cleveland, which had a six-game winning streak snapped on Wednesday, has a one-game lead over Chicago in the race for the division title. The White Sox own the division tiebreaker. ... “We know we control our own destiny still,” Guardians manager Stephen Vogt said. “So, I like where we are. We’ve got four games left, and we have a chance to get in. That’s all you can ask for.” ... Espino will serve as an opener for Cantillo, who will pitch in a bulk role. Cantillo is 10-9 with a 3.74 ERA this season. ... Cantillo is 1-0 with a 3.38 ERA in eight career innings against the Red Sox, and Espino has never faced Boston.
Cam Kerry can be reached at cam.kerry@globe.com.

item.title: [Spectrum News] Sonny Gray earns his 18th win as Red Sox beat Guardians 1-0
item.dc:creator: Associated Press
item.description: BOSTON (AP) — Sonny Gray pitched six innings to tie Philadelphia's Cristopher Sánchez for the major league lead with his 18th victory, Andruw Monasterio drove in the only run with a sixth-inning single, and the Boston Red Sox edged Cleveland 1-0 on Wednesday night to snap the Guardians' six-game winning streak. item.content:encoded:
BOSTON (AP) — Sonny Gray pitched six innings to tie Philadelphia's Cristopher Sánchez for the major league lead with his 18th victory, Andruw Monasterio drove in the only run with a sixth-inning single, and the Boston Red Sox edged Cleveland 1-0 on Wednesday night to snap the Guardians' six-game winning streak.
It was just the fifth win in 13 games for the Red Sox, who clinched a playoff spot on Sunday.
The 36-year-old Gray (18-5) is in line to become the fourth Red Sox pitcher since 2000 to lead the AL in victories, joining Rick Porcello (2016), Josh Beckett ('07) and Curt Schilling ('04).
Gray allowed four singles, struck out three, walked one and lowered his ERA to 2.72.
Aroldis Chapman struck out the side in the ninth for his 35th save of the season.
Cleveland starter Foster Griffin (15-6) gave up a run on 10 hits with seven strikeouts.
The Guardians entered with a one-game lead over the White Sox atop the AL Central after winning the series opener Tuesday, but needed a win Wednesday combined with a loss by either the Rangers or Astros to clinch a postseason berth.
The victory came with a price for the Red Sox when center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela left with right hamstring tightness after running out a single the same day he was activated from the injured list. He had been sidelined with a right a quad strain since Sept. 3 and made a diving headlong grab on Steven Kwan, the game's first batter.

item.title: [tsn.ca] Blue Jays finish season sitting 16th in MLB Power Rankings
item.dc:creator: ESPN
item.description: We’re down to the final days of the 2026 regular season with still quite a number of teams that have something to play for -- including a few who are fighting for their postseason lives.
